Name: Ad Astra
Review: I feel very calm after watching Ad Astra. That's pretty much all I can say. I'm gonna try and actually write some kind of review (or my thoughts, at least) because I honestly feel the film deserves it. Ad Astra did an amazing job of mirroring the calm, measured approach taken by the main character (Roy McBride) in most situations and I was pleasantly surprised by it, having gone into the film expecting an Interstellar-style romp across the solar system with the usual hurdles to overcome and plot devices to explore. Every scene had an air of tranquility to it, which I think worked wonders to reinforce Roy's personality upon us: unphased, calm and collected. Visually, Ad Astra was stunning. I think this might be my favourite space film if I had to rank them on wow-factor alone. I loved the futuristic yet realistic aesthetic of the spacecraft, stations and other technologies, as well as the beautiful planet shots as the film moved forwards. For some reason, this film really struck a chord with me and I felt compelled to write some stuff about it. Definitely recommend watching it if you haven't.

Review: "Charming" I think that's how I'd describe this film. The Vast of Night was an intense, atmospheric film that told a beautiful story and made me feel an excitement and nostalgia for an era before I'd even been born. So much is packed into its ninety minute timeframe that you'd expect the film to be fast-paced and energetic through and through; However, it's those moments when everything slows down - and to remember to breathe - that really made me fall in love with the unfolding story and its characters. Visually, The Vast of Night is really quite a beautiful film. It has a lot of the 50s neon and Midwestern architecture you'd expect from such a film, and the camera work feels so superbly tied to the action and motion on screen that I couldn't help but be drawn in and fixated until the very end. I didn't go into this film expecting to like it as much as I did, but I now cannot recommend it enough.

Name: Prospect
Review: There's something exhilarating about clunky, lo-fi science fiction. The technologies used are so close to current day counterparts that their weaknesses and limitations are still heavily apparent. In these movies the stakes are higher, the losses greater, and every tiny achievement - be it simply landing your drop pod, or retrieving a single rare gem - seems massive in comparison to the dangers you have to place yourself in just to survive. Prospect captures all of this and maybe more. I love science fiction, and I haven't been this engaged and interested in a film of this genre since Ad Astra which, looking back at, I would say contains a lot of similarities. Pedro Pascal is, unsurprisingly, very good in this, and I hope we get to see Sophie Thatcher in a lot more stuff to come! If I had to gripe about something, I would probably touch on the "indie-ness" of it a bit; the locations sometimes feel a bit too Earth-like (which is understandably tricky and probably unavoidable when working with a low budget), and it occasionally drew me out of the immersion and made me a bit too aware that I was watching some actors wander around in a Washington State rainforest. But, I don't like that I've written almost as many words on my negative thoughts as my positive, because that definitely isn't representative. Prospect is a very good movie and really recommend you watch it.

It felt just very flat all the way through, with no actual emotion or reason for me to care about any of the story or characters. Frankly, I was more interested in rooting for Oscar Isaac to take over Earth instead of the X-Men stopping him, which says a lot, I think. Glad I watched it, but only because I'm trying to watch all the X-Men films, and this was the second to last one standing in my way. Also, it's two and a half hours long. 😠

Name: Serenity
Review:
I really liked this! Haven't seen any Firefly, so I'll be watching that next and will perhaps then revisit and see what my thoughts are again.

It basically ticks all the boxes for what I enjoy in sci-fi, so that's a huge win.

Name: Logan Lucky
Review: I don't understand. It was so dull. I feel like it had everything a fun, exciting heist movie should have, and yet it was just not that.

Name: Greed
Review:
Tricky one, this...

I don't know whether I should be concerned by how well Coogan played the role of a mega-rich, super exploiting billionaire to be honest 😅

I definitely enjoyed this film; it was a fast-paced, punchy take on the modern day fast fashion industry shown through the actions of one selfish, hungry businessman. It's not hard to believe people like this exist in the real world. In fact, I'm pretty sure it's "based around" one Philip Green - give him a quick search!

However, Greed does fail to hit its mark a lot of the time. I think it would be a lot weaker without Coogan in the lead role, and I also feel some of the "social issues" brought up in the movie came across a bit last minute and tacked on (see: the docudrama-style end credits wall of text).

Name: Taxi
Review:
A fun action comedy! Pretty light on the story but overall a good time and worth a watch.

Bonus points for being in French, too.

Name: Headhunters
Review: I do love me a good Scandinavian film

Name: John Wick: Chapter 3 – Parabellum
Review: Definitely the weakest of the trilogy, I think. After a while all the gunfights and action sequences just begin to feel a but flat, despite the fact they're still some of the best in any movie I've seen. Too much of a good thing, perhaps?

Name: Sputnik
Review:
If you gave this to Hollywood, I honestly think they'd ruin it.

9/10 for most of it: the set design, the cinematography, the soundtrack, the acting. Really loved it!

I think it was just slightly let down by the story, as its pretty much a rehash of the "parasitic host takes over a person's body" trope.

Still very much worth a watch, though. Maybe you'll rate it higher!

Name: Redline
Review: Basically Speed Racer but even better!

Name: Locke
Review: Honestly, fuck Chicago.

Name: Limitless
Review:
This is such a filmbro movie.

And I hate to admit that I enjoyed it.

Name: Dredd
Review:
Felt a lot slower and less intense than the first time I watched it, but perhaps that's just because I knew what to expect going into it.

This movie is disappointingly Generic Action Movie in my opinion, especially because I really like the concept behind Dredd and wish it would expand a bit more into Mega City One, instead of trapping us inside a big tower block and rehashing The Raid (2011).

Holding out for a sequel...maybe...not.

Name: Hellboy
Review:
I feel like I should've enjoyed this more than I did.

Helloby is a really likeable character, but there was just no reason for me to feel invested in anything that happened!
I think the villains could've be improved a lot, as a clockwork Nazi that spins its swords around lots just doesn't really cut it (choosing to ignore Rasputin and his 101 Hellhounds because they really are just inconsequential to the entire storyline).

Name: The Other Guys
Review: Not really my kind of thing but I can see why people would enjoy it

Name: Hellboy II: The Golden Army
Review: Miles, MILES, better than the first one! Very del Toro, very engaging, and very good!

Name: The Dig
Review: Carey Mulligan please may I marry you?

Name: Sorry to Bother You
Review:
One of the weirdest movies I've ever seen, and unlike anything I've watched before. And somehow, it still manages to be good!
Big supporter of the horseplay in this one 😊

Name: Darkman
Review: Mmmm no. No thank you.

Name: Hope Gap
Review: It's a risky move making one of your main characters so manipulative, provocative, toxic and unlikeable in every way. I'm this movie's case, it didn't pay off. I fucking hate Bening's character with every fibre of my being and I'm annoyed I had to watch 1h40m of her on-screen. Bill Nighy was clever to get away when he could, and Josh O'Connor should've stayed in London. This was such a non-movie.

Name: Greenland
Review: POV: You are Gerard Butler and you singlehandedly decimate an entire United States Air Force base's evacuation plans by going back for your son's insulin.

Name: Arlington Road
Review:
Very much enjoying reading all the 1-star Amazon reviews complaining about it not having a classic "good guy beats bad guy" Hollywood ending.

My expectations were successfully subverted. Really enjoyed this movie.

Name: X-Men: First Class
Review: Gee, I wonder what made me want to watch this movie again. I think I had a vision that some of the characters in it were going to become important again in the near future? --- Pretty good X-Men film overall, I'd say. Definitely one of my favourites. McAvoy and Fassbender as Xavier and Magneto are really, really good in my opinion, and a damn sight better than those old codgers that were cast in the first movie (I jest 😉)

Name: Hotel Artemis
Review:
Despite the strong cast and (quite) cool premise, this film just kind of washed over me. ~*Events transpired*~

Was very cool to see Zachary Quinto again, ngl.

Name: The Spy Gone North
Review: I didn't understand most of it, but the vibes were good

Name: I Care a Lot
Review: I think it probably was a good movie, yeah. Was spoilt for me by the women vs. men dynamic which ran throughout and really just felt shoehorned in for the sake of it.

Name: What If
Review:
A pretty simple, funny, heartwarming romance. Maybe a bit shallow in some places?
Either way it made me feel all the emotions I wanted to feel going in, so yeah, I had a good time :) 

Also bonus points for surprise Mackenzie Davis, and Adam Driver (unsurprisingly) stealing the show.

Name: The Garden of Words
Review: One of the most beautifully-animated animes I've ever seen, rivalled only by Your Name. Heartbreaking yet hopeful, this definitely worth watching, and it packs a surprising amount in its 45 minute runtime. --- I read some other people's reviews and let myself be influenced by their opinions. It's definitely not as profound as it tries to be, and there are a few things that are quite difficult to look past when enjoying the film (namely a pretty sizeable, and questionable, age gap between the two characters). Idk, I still enjoyed it but I completely see where everyone else is coming from.

Name: Coco
Review: Not ashamed to say I cried a few times while watching this. Movies with a focus on the importance of music (amongst other things) have a special place in my heart, and Coco serves a demonstration of how it can bring families together and repair old relationships, no matter how "broken" they are.

Name: Inside Man
Review: I really enjoyed this! I'm struggling to put my thoughts into words because I'm terrible at writing reviews and am in no way qualified for longform. It's tense, it's enthralling, it's meticulously-crafted, and yet somehow also manages an ocassional air of levity and humour to perfectly balance it out. Go into this expecting a good film, and you'll be greatly rewarded.

Name: Sound of Metal
Review: I was considering giving this 4 stars, but then I took a look at the other movies I'd recently given the same rating, and I read some other people's reviews, and I realised it definitely deserved higher. Sound of Metal masterfully depicts the struggle of such a life-changing event, and how Riz Ahmed's character has to suffer, learn to cope with, and, in some ways, ultimately come to appreciate his new way of living life. There were some truly crushing moments in this for me, and the entire film is supported by one hell of an incredible cast. I also want to applaud this film's sound design for so eloquently depicting what it would be like to be in Ruben's position. Probably my top watch of 2021 so far. --- Also, I watched the first half of this movie without subtitles, before thinking that it might possibly be a good idea to turn them on in case it shed any light on the sign language used throughout. In my opinion, it didn't really add anything, so if you can do without then you won't miss out.

Name: Sully
Review: Movies like this always, always hit me really hard emotionally, and Sully was no exception. It's not quite on par with Captain Phillips in terms of its story or scale, but Hanks was talented as always and overall I really enjoyed it.

Name: Zero Dark Thirty
Review: Whenever there's a story about Al Qaeda, terrorism, bin Laden, the American military, there's a risk that a movie will go full yee-haw gung-ho and glamorise the crap out it. I so glad Zero Dark Thirty didn't. As far as I could tell, ZDT was simply a gritty, on-the-nose retelling of events (from a US perspective, of course) following the hunt for Osama bin Laden and the people behind it. This is an epic tale spanning many years, and I really appreciated the division of the film into lots of little "acts", all of which culminate in the thirty minute, near silent finale which is an incredible payoff for an already incredible movie. Chastain was perfect in her role, and I couldn't imagine many other people who could take her place as lead and display the same focus and determination she did. Honestly, and I know this is probably the point, everyone else was very incidental and only served as characters to play off and interact with hers. But I think that worked really well. 100% must-watch if you haven't seen it already. It hits somewhat differently after having literally watched The Report the day before, too. Not sure why I'm only giving it a 7/10, though. I think I'm going through a phase of doubting my own opinions.

Name: WandaVision
Review: Really wasn't a fan of this show to be honest. I don't know if I just missed out on what everyone else loved about it, or if it was an Emperor's New Clothes situation but I just feel like there was so much build up in the first few episodes...and for what? Basically nothing of any note. The finale was a massive let down and I honestly believe you could skip the entire show and not miss out when you come to watch any of the Phase Four Marvel movies. I don't think that's a great sign for the quality of a TV series. p.s. Don't even get me started on the episode lengths and the amount of credits in each. Maybe I would've enjoyed it more if I'd waited and binged it all in one go.

Name: Punch-Drunk Love
Review:
Boy does PTA know how to make a weird film!

I doubt I gave this as much attention as I ought to have done, so it probably deserves a rewatch at some point.

Name: The Place Beyond the Pines
Review:
1st part: yes
2nd part: no
3rd part: yes

Name: Raya and the Last Dragon
Review: Easily the most visually impressive and stunningly animated movie I've ever seen. I really loved the first half's "episodic" style, and the soundtrack wasn't half bad either. Raya's story isn't anything to write home about, though; it felt pretty cookie-cutter in its themes of loss, unification, trust, and humanity. However, that's almost to be expected from a Disney movie, and I went into it expecting as much, so I wasn't even disappointed.

Name: The Game
Review: Holy. Fucking. Shit. What an incredible movie! I had a huge, stupid grin plastered across my huge, stupid face the entire time. Incredible sense of mystery, unease, and paranoia throughout, and honesty I had no clue as to what was really the truth right the way through to end.

Name: Elizabeth
Review: I would accept Cate Blanchett as my queen

Name: The Shining
Review: Gripping from start to finish. I forgot how amazing this movie was, and I'm so glad I watched it a second time. Gonna be following it up with Doctor Sleep straight away becuase I think it'll be really cool.

Name: Doctor Sleep
Review: Yes! This is good shit! This is a great sequel! I really liked how this actually continued on the story from The Shining, and introduced its own, new ideas, without also being a re-hash of the previous movie (or adding new "lore" which doesn't already kind of work with the world set out). It's been ages since I've seen Ewan McGregor act in anything, and I really missed him!

Name: Mississippi Grind
Review: It took me so long to finish this movie. I started it three or four days ago, got distracted by something else halfway through, and then just couldn't find any reasons or motivation to finish watching it (other than so I could get it off my Plex and free up some space (1TB hard drive gang wya?)). I didn't really enjoy Mississippi Grind as much as I was expecting. I'd seen people describing it as a "buddy film" and I guess that made me go into it expecting something a little more upbeat. Instead, I got a story about the depressing outcomes of a gambling addiction and a journey across midwestern(?) America - I know there's a lot more to analyse about this movie but I'm too pea-brained to do so myself. Mendelsohn and Reynolds are both very good in it, though, but I'm struggling to find much more to say really. I guess I just found it overall a bit of a...grind. *audience groans*

Name: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
Review: Pretty excited for this show! Will try and update with a score for each episode here. Episode 1: 6/10 Pretty setup-heavy and felt quite like Phase 1 Marvel, which I liked. Introduced a bunch of characters early on and I'll be interested to see who sticks around for the whole series. Episode 2: 5/10 Something definitely feels off about this series to me so far, but I can't quite place what it is. I think the story's getting off to a weak start, and I'm not sure where it's planning on going; it feels far too generic and not really linked enough to anything that "Marvel" at the moment. Glad to see the relationship between Bucky and Sam fleshed out a little bit and new Cap has the potential to become a more interesting character, I hope. Episode 3: 7/10 Definitely feels like the story is coming together more now, or maybe I'm just finally understanding what's going on. Madripoor looks very cool, and I really hope we get to see more of it this series! Karli is still giving off a bit too much "angsty teenager" energy for my liking but hopefully that subsides a bit in the coming episodes because it makes it hard for me to care about her mission at the moment. Episode 4: 8/10 Best episode so far! I'm writing this a good few days after I watched it, so my thoughts aren't that fresh, but some really interesting character arcs are beginning to form and I think that's going to make for a very good second half of the show. Episode 5: 8/10 Damn lol, the Flag Smashers really aren't that scary a villain that have in a show like this. Ooh, spooky, they cause flash mobs of people and blow stuff up but are otherwise just small-to-medium-level terrorists? And their leader is just a teenage girl with Angst? Maybe that's the point? I don't know. Glad to see Sam and Bucky acknowledge that they'll never be as close with each other as they were with Steve, and I think that was a big turning for them and for us seeing them in future shows. Also a massive "hell yeah" that Sam is picking up the mantle!!! Episode 6: 6/10 Quite a disappointing finale to the series, although I don't really know what other direction it could've gone in. Very much hoping that's it for the Flag Smashers because, while their political motives are at least interesting, they're in no way cut out for being a full-scale Big Bad Evil (not that I think anyone's saying that).

Name: Zack Snyder's Justice League
Review: I never watched Whedon's Justice League so I suppose I have no point of comparison but I genuinely really enjoyed the Snyder Cut. It actually felt like the movie used its four-hour runtime effectively, for the most part, and there weren't many points where I wish it had sped up or skipped over any scenes (a lot of those moments were concentrated nesrter the end, to be honest). I think DC has managed to carve out a pretty decent spot from Marvel's (pretty sizeable) monopoly on the superhero movie market, setting itself apart as something a bit darker and more gritty; the fights are stronger, the lu ches hit harder, and I kind of felt like the characters cared a bit more, too. Maybe I've just been missing my fix of mainstream supe movies, though, so who knows? If I had to pick out some things which I wasn't as much a fan of, I'd definitely go for the easy targets and complain about the over-use of slow-mo scenes (and also how long each one was!), as well as DC's inability to use any colours other than black, blue, and orange. I get that they're probably aiming for a consistent theme throughout they're movies but a bit more of the colour wheel would be greatly appreciated.

Name: Kick-Ass
Review: Sad to waste two hours of my life watching this, only to realise I've already seen it!

Name: Aniara
Review:
Hard to know how to rate this one.

Definitely depressing, and I'm sure there's some symbolism in it about humanity inevitably destroying whichever host it lives on, and us needing to be grateful for (and take better care of) Earth.

Name: Logan's Run
Review:
Jessica: "Oh it's so cold! Maybe we can wrap these [animal furs] around us to keep us warm."

Logan: "Yes, but first let's take our clothes off before they freeze us!"

Logan, you cheeky bugger!

Name: Fargo
Review:
I can see why it's the sort of film people would rate highly but I didn't quite gel with it as much.

Glad to have finally watched it, though.

Name: Shazam!
Review: This film has such a strong first half but I feel like it's completely let down by a very weak and cheesy final act. Levi is great as Shazam! and all of interactions between him and Freddie are a joy to watch. Just not too keen on the whole, "there's a whole family of Shazams now" stuff (even though I know it was in the comics). Obviously very different to DC's Snyderverse, and I can't imagine they'd try and merge the two...that would be very strange ngl.

Name: The Maze Runner
Review:
I'm watching the Maze Runner trilogy because I'm desperate to know the story but don't fancy reading the books (and the Wikipedia synopsis is cheating). 

Fully expecting the following two movies to be utterly crap but this one really isn't too bad! As far as the storyline goes it's definitely interesting, and the cinematography and CGI are impressive enough too. I think the soundtrack could've been better, though, as it felt far too generic with a distinct lack of thought put in to creating a unique and appropriate atmosphere.

Overall, though, yeah. Not bad!

Name: Maze Runner: The Scorch Trials
Review: My favourite part was when Thomas said, "What is this? Some kind of Scorch Trial?"

Name: Face/Off
Review: Ridiculous, daft, and over-the-top in all the best ways! Travolta and Cage play their roles amazingly as arch-nemeses and I had a blast all the way from start to finish. One of Cage's best performances, I think, even if he did spend most of it as John Travolta.

Name: Page Eight
Review: The kind of movie where you watch the entire 1h40m runtime, and there's still 20 minutes left to go. Also, Paul Englishby has the audacity to write two incredible pieces of jazz for the start and end of this movie and not release them anywhere for me to listen to afterwards!

Name: Maze Runner: The Death Cure
Review: Honestly some of the most generic, uninspired drivel I've ever had the displeasure of watching. Death Cure is all explosions, gunfire and shattered glass with no substance to back it up, coupled with every trope you could expect from a YA Sci-fi book turned movie. And they didn't even have the decency to keep Newt alive to the end. 😡

Name: Spectral
Review:
Take a shot every time someone says some variation of, "move it" or, "let's go!"

Really aggressively mediocre story and acting, but surprisingly good CGI!

Name: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
Review: I didn't enjoy this as much as I was hoping. And I was really hoping it was going to be amazing. When we watched the first episode all my friends bemoaned the fact it felt like we'd gone straight back to Phase One Marvel, with none of the crazy, wacky, magical multiverse stuff that WandaVision set up and basically worked off. Personally I wasn't too bothered by it and welcomed something a bit more "grounded in reality" instead of being too unbelievable. But boy oh boy, though, this shit got dull fast! I've become so used to Phase Three Marvel that watching a bunch of strong people punch each other and run around warehouses has become really dull! I did like the political and humanitarian sides of this show, though, because I don't really feel like Marvel has taken the time to address them in anything else of theirs yet. Not sure I'm qualified to assess how well they covered them but I at least feel like it was taken seriously, sensitively and with the best of intentions? Looking back I definitely enjoyed WandaVision more, which I'm surprising myself by saying, but FATW is definitely worth at least a 6/10 overall. Praying for Loki to blow these previous two shows out of the water, ngl.

Name: Stowaway
Review: Not quite the Sci-fi thriller I was expecting, but overall a very competent movie.

Name: Nobody
Review:
Glad I watched it, and the first half or so felt very novel and entertaining!

Was let down a little bit in the second half with the classic "evil Russians" cliche and the budding up with old friends trope, which just led to it all feeling a bit hollow for me.

Odenkirk is absolutely great, though, and I really need to see him in more stuff! Might even have to put myself through Breaking Bad so I can then watch Better Call Saul or something.

Name: Giri/Haji
Review: Yeah, this is good. Like, really good. It's refreshingly different to your average drama, with some really imaginative cinematography, a beautiful multi-culturalness, and a well thought out, intricately woven storyline.

Name: The History of Future Folk
Review: Definitely not what I was expecting - especially with the incredibly misleading poster that Netflix showed me - but it had its moments of whimsical charm. The music was the best part of this, which is good I suppose, given that it's one of the main focusses of the movie. Aside from that though, I felt like the storyline was pretty weak and it kind of fell weirdly somewhere between "indie musical" and "low budget comedy".

Name: Take Shelter
Review: Honestly very powerful, and it spoke to me in some way I can't really explain. Shannon and Chastain both give amazing performances in this, and I'd be really pressed to find something I disliked.

Name: The Year Earth Changed
Review:
Really heartwarming, and a welcome change of pace from all the doom and gloom in the news at the moment.

It is depressing, however, to think/know that as soon as everything opens back up again life will go straight back to normal again and no-one will really bat an eyelid at the recoveries made by the planet and its species in our absence. Seeing how quickly the air pollution in some cities reduced once the roads emptied out was incredible; who'd have thought the Himalayas had been hidden behind that massive cloud of smog all this time!?

I hope enough people watch this because it was really good. Nature is healing and we are the virus.

Name: The Way Back
Review:
Ben Affleck is very good as usual! No surprises there, though.

Would've liked to see his personal battles interleaved a bit more with those of the basketball team, rather than them being split into very obvious segments, and the soundtrack could probably sound a little less generic?

Overall, though, I though this was a really solid movie!

Name: Molly's Game
Review: It was fine. They definitely tried to hype it up by getting Jessica Chastain to narrate a bunch of fast-paced poker games and it worked because they were the most interesting bits!

Name: Dawn of the Planet of the Apes
Review: The soundtrack and cinematography in this are absolutely amazing. I don't think Dawn is as good as Rise but it certainly nabs the second spot with ease.

Name: Promising Young Woman
Review: Hmm, yeah... Interesting! I'm not quite sure what my thoughts are on this one, because I didn't hate it but I also didn't like it all that much either. It felt quite unsure in its footing, especially the first half, and was nowhere near as polished as I thought it would be. Carey Mulligan is, unsurprisingly, amazing in her role and Burnham is...okay, I guess? I haven't seen him before in anything so this was his acting debut for me. Everyone else, however, felt like single-use characters, used solely for the purpose of moving a scene forward. I think the storyline had a lot of potential and I was a little disappointed with how it ended, too. Would've liked to see it fleshed out more, although maybe that would be hard for an admittedly small-scale revenge flick like this - I think that's what frustrates me slightly: it could've been so much more, and had a much larger, emotional impact than it did.

Name: A Quiet Place
Review: Basically as good as I remember! Shame about the people across the aisle from me who decided the best use of their £16 ticket was to provide each other with a running commentary all the way through. It's crazy how much respect A Quiet Place demands from its viewers, in terms of sitting as silently as possible, carefully eating their snacks to avoid crackling the packaging and incurring wrath of all the other moviegoers. And everyone complies! Can't wait to watch the second part!

Name: A Quiet Place Part II
Review: Just as good as the first one, I would say. It definitely helped that I went to a back-to-back screening of the two movies (thank you Everyman for hosting it), and that Part II picks things up from pretty much exactly where the original left them. Cooler setpieces, more characters, more story, more monsters! It's exactly what I'd hoped it would be.

Name: The Daytrippers
Review:
I felt a connection to this movie on a really compelling level.

This story taking place over the course of a single day in 90s New York, filled with a cast of eccentric caricatures and set to a wonderfully breezy yet emotional soundtrack make for an extremely authentic-feeling setting - one which I'd love nothing more than to be able to live in and experience for myself. 

The acting felt a little ropey at some points, especially near the beginning, but that to added to this film's charm for me. There were some lovely comparisons of similarity between different characters, too, which I would love to keep an eye out for again on another watch!

Schreiber absolutely stole every scene he was in, with the "educated, overly self-important writer" role he plays.

Name: Demon Slayer -Kimetsu no Yaiba- The Movie: Mugen Train
Review: Literal chills. Demon Slayer is an incredible series in many ways, and Mugen Train serves as a great accompaniment to - and continuation of - the TV anime. In the space of just two hours we're treated to a great story, emotional character development, and some of the most wonderfully-crafted fight sequences I've ever seen, all coupled with the same amazing animation, sound design and soundtrack that made Season 1 so popular. Highly recommend watching this if you've finished the first season of Demon Slayer, and I massively recommend watching the first season of Demon Slayer if you still haven't seen that!

Name: Soul
Review:
I enjoyed this even more the second time around!

Stunningly animated, beautifully scored, and it tells a really powerful, emotive story that perhaps caters more to older viewers than younger audiences, which is a really good move I think.

Name: Piper
Review: Head empty. No thoughts, only piper.

Name: Little Miss Sunshine
Review: You've gotta love a big family dance number.

Name: The Wolverine
Review: It feels kinda weird to see Wolverine in a movie with any reference to X-Men whatsoever, but I don't think it was bad by any stretch. The action sequences were really fun (especially the bullet train) and I appreciate how Wolverine's abilities are beginning to be framed more as a curse of life now. It sets up the theme for movies like Logan really well. I do think it was probably a little long for my liking, and the final act was definitely quite anticlimactic but it overall it was a good watch and a neat addition to the X-Men series (even though it basically has very little bearing on any of the other movies)!

Name: The Devil Wears Prada
Review: I have no idea when I watched this but I saw a trailer and instantly knew that I definitely did at some point, and had a great time too!

Name: Haywire
Review: It's a competent spy thriller, but it's also just a bit dull. Carano really doesn't look like she's putting any effort into her acting whatsoever, and comes across incredibly wooden and uncaring for the duration of the movie. The story is bland and uninteresting (and also a bit confusing), which is a shame because the cast has so much potential (McGregor and Fassbender!?) and I just feel like they're not utilised at all to do anything extraordinary! The film is perforated with these long moments of silence, with or without dialogue, and I feel like Soderbergh was aiming to use these to inject tension and emotion into the scenes, when really all they achieve is a sense of awkwardness instead... The cinematography and soundtrack, on the other hand, are really quite good. David Holmes's score is jazzy, intriguing and mysterious, and Soderbergh frames his shots beautifully and really works to make every shot interesting. The fight scenes were also surprisingly good! They lack all of the intensity and punch of Hollywood action movies and are instead are full of long cuts and brutal choreography which serves really well in conveying their realism and keeping them feeling grounded. Probably worth a watch, especially since its only an hour and a half long.

Name: No Sudden Move
Review: Stylistically, everything about this was on point, but damn if the story didn't fly over my head a bit. I think I'll need to watch it again sometime to fully appreciate it. Soderbergh's decision to film everything through a fisheye was a choice, too. Feel like my eyes did me a runner whenever there was a long panning shot (spoiler alert: there were many)

Name: The Tomorrow War
Review: I'm really sorry but I actually quite enjoyed this movie! It's a Hollywood cheese-fest turned up to 11 but it does it so well and feels so gratifying to watch. Aliens that shoot spikes from 5-meter long tentacles on their backs? Mental. Swarms of said aliens climbing up the sides of buildings? Mental. Hand-to-hand combat with the Alien Queen on the edge of an arctic precipice? Fucking mental. I had a lot of fun and I'm not ashamed to say it.

Name: The Great Gatsby
Review:
Honestly fuck it this movie is so dull and Di Caprio says "old sport" so much I want to off myself

The only redeeming part is Carrie Mulligan.

Name: The Talented Mr. Ripley
Review: Utterly gripping, and hauntingly beautiful. I enjoyed this movie far more than I expected I would, and was drawn in by its incredible cast and deeply interesting story. Struggling to actually write a proper review because, well, I'm bad at writing reviews but I would definitely watch again. Matt Damon honestly does some of his best acting here, and it's my headcanon that the end of this movie ties directly into the beginning of The Bourne Identity

Name: The Informant!
Review: An shockingly unbelievable story which grows and grows and spirals out of control as the movie progresses and the pieces of the puzzle fall into place. Soderbergh perfectly combines the serious content matter of an investagtion into corporate fraud and embezzlement with the levity of an upbeat, almost slapstic sountrack to create a truly unique and enjoyable movie! Matt Damon is, unsurprisngly, the linchpin of the entire film, carrying it from scene to scene with some really great acting and once again proving how talented he is at playing a huge range of different characters - I recently watched The Talented Mr Ripley and you'd almost think his parts were cast to two different people. I really enjoyed this!

Review: Prometheus kind of reminds me of the Cloverfield "trilogy" in the sense that it really feels like this could've been a standalone film at first, with the Alien parts tacked on at the last minute to tie it to something more substantial and perhaps help with ticket sales on release day. If it weren't directed by Ridley Scott himself then I think I'd really be entertaining that train of thought. Visually, I really enjoyed this. It's modern enough to have great CGI and combines that with sweeping vistas and some nice practical effects to create a movie which feels like a realistic and upgraded version of the orignal Alien. The story, on the other hand, is pretty dire. It's hard to believe that a company spending $1 trillion would hire a crew of such incompetent people and feel comfortable sending them off to be the first people to meet humanity's creators. Because of this, it's no fun watching all the terrible things that happen to them because...you can completely see it coming? It would be much cooler to watch an actual, functioning team of people do everything right and still just get absolutely wrecked by the monstrosities created by those Engineers. There are also far too many questions left unanswered (some of which I'm not sure were done intentionally) with the only solace being that a few of them are answered a little bit more in the Alien: Covenant (or as I like to call it, Alien: Convent - how cool would it be to have a movie with a bunch of Xenomorphs running around dressed like nuns??)

Name: Lost in Translation
Review: This movie really had to make me going and feel emotions, huh? Wamth, fuzziness, happiest, sadness, loneliness, hopefulness, all the things. I sat for a bit, just watching the credits roll, to give myself time to process it. If nothing else, I really empathised with the feelings of being stuck in an unfamiliar place, all by yourself, without people around you as a network to spend time with and lean on when you need support. Lost in Translation expertly translates that lyrical loneliness into film and I'm equal parts glad and upset I was able to relive it again. There's a beautiful romance that blossoms between Murray and Johansson's characters, two kindred spirits at very different stages of their lives who find each other in the noise and bright lights of a sleepless city in a foreign country. Their relationship flowers as they share their nights together, not necessarily in a romantic way at first but as a mutual kind of love for each other - two people experiencing the same emotions of loss, loneliness and, above all else, an uncertainty about their place and purpose in the world. This relationship is overshadowed and made all the more fragile by the knowledge that its destined to end, to fail, that within the week they will be forced apart from one another, pulled away from their brief period of respite and thrust back into the lives they so desperately want to escape. The second half is definitely where this movie's strengths lie, for me, but I think that makes sense given the first half is used very effectively to set everything up. Murray and Johansson both perform amazingly in this, and the atmosphere and emotion throughout is really, really, very good.

As mentioned, though, it's hard to see past what essentially feels like a "good vs. bad" undertone stretching throughout the entire film. Clearly we're supposed to see the police as a force for good in the fight against London's estate-dwelling, violent, drug-riddled youth, but I think the dialogue around that is much more nuanced that is represented here. Definitely worth keeping this in mind when watching, because I caught myself more times than I expected actually rooting against the "heroes" of this story and siding with the "villains". If that's intentional then bravo, I think that's a good move.

Anyway, I was expecting a Kingsman movie, and I got something much better. I enjoyed this.

Review: How on earth did this actually meet my insanely sky-high expectations????? Denis I will forever be in your debt. Honestly just incredible in every way I can think of: - First of, it seems like a really faithful adaptation to me. I've read the first book and can't think of a single thing I would do differently in this Part 1 movie. Dune is famously heralded as "un-adaptable" but I really think Villeneuve has achieved it. - The film is visually stunning. You know how everyone keeps saying, "find the biggest screen you can, and watch Dune on it"? Well they're 100% right. You just need to. It's amazing! It's massive, bold, colourful, awesome, and jaw-dropping in many, many ways. - Hans Zimmer's score is potentially my favourite part. He's created such a rich sound filled with motifs that permeate every part of the movie, and it sounds so authentic and native to Arrakis, which I think is incredible. The sound design is also mindblowing, and I'm actually incredibly tempted to buy a ticket just so I can experience the Sardaukar planet scene again.

Is that the point, that it's a mish-mash of both and kind of supposed to be all over the place and I'm just bad for not being able to appreciate it? Perhaps. This was a really great movie to start my Christmas holidays with. I enjoyed its relatively small-scale environment - I'm a sucker for "it all takes place in one room" movies - I loved the atmosphere built up through the dialogue and sound design, and it had an incredibly satisfying third act which I just think was really, really good.

Name: Wrath of Man
Review: Guy Ritchie makes films for Real Men who like shouting and swearing and fucking and killing, and they need to be all about men and guns and money and guns, and women aren't allowed to be in it unless they're fridged or fucked or killed—unless it's a masculine woman, then it's okay for her to have one line about a man's dick size—and the dialogue has to solely consist of grunts and swearing and quips and hollow one-liners that don't actually mean anything. They all need to be exactly two hours long and consist of three very well-defined acts culminating in the Good Guy—who isn't really good because he's still a gangster but he's better than the other gangsters because they kill more people and are rude—exacting a good amount of premeditated revenge on the Bad Guy and we have to feel triumphant about that fact, as the movie ends with a slow fade on our Good Guy and the credits roll to some funky, hip-hop music. And yet, despite saying all this and being aware of all this, I still enjoyed watching Wrath of Man. Nowhere near as much as The Gentlemen or Snatch, which both oozed that quintessential Guy Ritchie flair and style, but I still thought it was fine. The change of pace to a much more serious, straightforward approach was engaging, and I was genuinely intrigued by the plot as bits of it were slowly revealed as the film progressed.

Name: Dune
Review: Watching this again really just reminded me how much I love this movie, and the fact that I found the same scenes equally as jaw-dropping and awe-inspiring as the first time I saw it is testament to the quality of the world Villeneuve has managed to create in his visualisation of Dune. It's pure, clean science fiction—my favourite sort—with the added bonuses of great political drama and events transpiring on a galactic scale. The praise here is probably better attributed to Herbert's original novel but I think Villeneuve did an incredible job of translating it to film, at least compared to Lynch's attempt—although that's not a very high bar—and definitely having read the first book and knowing how everything plays out. It's hard to deny that this is really just a setup film for Dune: Part 2, but I would wholly disagree with anybody who uses that argument as a reason for docking stars because I think this two and a half hour exhibition-fest was (a) extremely well-paced and meticulously crafted, and (b) entirely necessary for the next movie to carry any sort of weight whatsoever. Definitely getting another 9/10 from me, and I'm really looking forward to the next one!

Review: Not sure it quite lived up to my expectations but I had a good time! Kimi is essentially a pretty competent "Covid Zoom movie" cum action thriller which somehow manages to mention Covid in a way that feels completely natural and doesn't make the movie about Covid. I didn't find the story particularly interesting, to be honest, and the soundtrack felt very slapped on at the last minute; there were multiple points in the movie where the soundtrack just did not mesh with what was happening on screen - and also one part where I really think it should've been complete silence instead. Kravitz was really good, and I'm very jealous of her apartment. Wonder what the rent must be for a place like that.

Name: Flee
Review: It's very hard to know how to rate something like this. "Five stars," is my first instinct but I think it would be a disservice to reduce such an upsetting, emotional, inspiring piece of art to just a single number - at least not without talking more about why it deserves such praise. I think a large reason I liked this so much was simply the huge disconnect and unfamiliarity with basically all of the subject matter and themes covered in the film. It sounds counterintuitive, I know, but somehow it helped me relate to - and understand - Amin so much more, fully removing myself from my shoes, and completely stepping into his. I feel like I have a lot more I want to say about this film but I'm very much struggling to put it into words.

Review: The colours. Oh my gosh, the colours! To be honest, I didn't care all that much for this film's story or message but that didn't stop it from being visually gorgeous; every scene was so vibrant, and every environment so alive!

Name: The Last Duel
Review: Boy oh boy, this really grew on me as I kept watching. The retelling of events from each perspective was handled very well, with each one adding an extra layer to the - already uncertain - truth, constantly challenging the viewer to pick a side and person to believe. The duel at the end was simply incredible; I haven't seen a fight on-screen like that in while, and the intensity bled right through the screen (no pun intended) to fill the room I was in. I do feel the ending could've been a little better wrapped up, since the "truth" is left rather ambiguous, but, perhaps that's the point? I doubt any single retelling covers all the facts with perfect accuracy 👀

Name: Layer Cake
Review: Bro it's just dull. Spending the first 15 minutes info-dumping and listing a bunch of characters' names only works if you're Guy Ritchie, or The Big Short directed by Adam McKay; this film is neither of those. I actually gave up watching it because I just didn't care for what was happening and I wanted to spend my evening doing other, more exciting, things instead. At least it looked stylish.

Name: Jerry Maguire
Review: I really enjoyed this! While technically a rom-com (I think), I didn't find it too soppy or cheesy, and the humour was a perfect balance between blink-and-you-miss-it background gags and wonderfully dry, clever quips that catch you off-guard and land really well; Laurel's entire character feels constructed around this and she's great. Tom Cruise was as Cruisey as ever, which I personally don't mind. I enjoyed his acting and the role suited him well. His relationship with Rod had such a satisfying journey, and made for a perfect conclusion to the story. I wish it was a little shorter, though. Two and a bit hours was stretching it a bit, and you could definitely feel the length (uwu)

Name: Rain Man
Review: It's not often that I feel that burning, visceral hatred for a character in a movie, but Tom Cruise managed to evoke it within me. And that's great; I think it's a sign of some really good acting. Dustin Hoffman also deserved way more than an Oscar nomination for his role. I can't speak for how accurate his portrayal of someone with autism was but it definitely felt authentic and tastefully handled. The soundtrack absolutely slaps, too.

Name: The Firm
Review: Thus concludes the Cruise Cruise - three Tom Cruise movies in three days. My takeaways from this epic excursion? Tom Cruise was in some great movies when he was younger, and he's a great actor! I feel bad that he's been typecast into such an action hero role nowadays because he has so much more potential range outside of, essentially, Mission Impossible. This move itself was probably my least favourite of the trio I watched. I definitely felt the 2h34 runtime and think maybe half an hour could've been shaved off without anything too important being missed. The Firm lacked intensity for me, I think. Nothing felt that high-stakes or tense, despite it being seemingly written that way. Actions had consequences, sure, but I didn't really care? And the events leading to the third act were just a bit dull. But yeah, Tom Cruise was good. Maybe he should've taken one of those job offers on Wall Street instead after all.

Name: A Cure for Wellness
Review: My oh my, what a goofy ahh movie. The first act was really good, I'll say that. I loved the mystery shrouding everything, and I loved trying to figure out what was going on (because it was clear something dodgy was haopening) but after that, the movie was just a mess for me. First and foremost, it's way too long. Could've easily been 2h and just as good, maybe even shorter. The feeds into my other main problem which is mainly just that Things are revealed far too disparately and at such a slow pace. The number of scenes where Lockhart learns a new Thing by walking into a secret room and slowly pacing around it...i don't have enough fingers. And the ending. Oh, the ending. So out of pocket hahaha. Everything wraps up in like half an hour of the goofiest writing I've seen in a while, and it's super unsatisfying (but no less hilarious and amusing). I will say, though, there's one scene in the final third of the movie which made me feel really, like incredibly, ill. Points for that, I suppose. This movie is like Midsommar's older, but much less attractive, cousin.

Name: Atlantis: The Lost Empire
Review: Maybe I expected too much from a simple Disney animation but almost everything about this was completely unremarkable. The story and writing were both incredibly cookie-cutter, filled to the brim with too many characters and not enough character development, and pumped full of clichéd lines and uninteresting dialogue. If you have even half a brain cell you'll be able to predict where the story's heading right from the get-go; I know this was written for kids but it's been proven time and time again that it's possible for movies like this to age well even when adults watch them. The animation was great though, to be fair. I think it had a little bit of that "3D-but-2D" stuff that was used a lot in Futurama and it definitely added a lot of fluidity and depth to the movie, which is good given how much of it was set underwater! Anyway, I don't know why I wrote such a serious review for such a non-serious movie. Treasure Island is better than this. Go watch that instead. Or maybe Sinbad. I remember Sinbad being amazing.

Name: Sinbad: Legend of the Seven Seas
Review: I lived and breathed this movie as a child, and I still genuinely think holds up to this day. The pacing feels absolutely perfect to me, and so much happens in just a 1h30 runtime without the movie feeling rushed or sloppy. I picked up on a lot more gags than I did when I was younger too, which made the entire experience even more fun! Also Eris 😵😵

Name: Werewolf by Night
Review:
What a strange thing for Marvel to just drop (I think) out of nowhere?? That's not to say I didn't enjoy it, though.

I really liked the first half, up to the end of the hunt, and thought the acting and cinematography were great! I don't know if they shot this on actual film but I spotted a few cigarette stubs on the screen at the end of some scenes, which was cute.

The charm basically vanished for me in the second half, though, where it felt like the production team just started trying to answer the question, "what if Marvel movie, but in black and white?" For me, this resulted in the feeling of something being missing (namely, any colour whatsoever) rather than the creation of an eerie atmosphere. I don't think Marvel action scenes work great on ye olde film.

Still thought it was pretty great, though! Giacchino crushed it with the soundtrack, too.

At least in comparison to Knives Out, everything felt a bit underdeveloped and façade-like.

Name: Barbarian
Review: Safest neighbourhood in Detroit. --- For my serious review, though, I first want to say that I was really, really prepared to rate this higher; consider this an extremely generous 7/10, mainly due to how much I loved the first half. I thought Barbarian started incredibly strongly, with an intriguing premise and great acting by Campbell and Skarsgård. I was so very invested in the relationship between their characters, looking forward to how it would develop over the course of the movie. What a fool I was. I can pinpoint the moments in this movie where I went from enjoying it to merely entertaining it, to basically suffering through it, which is a real shame. So many scenes in the final act felt cheap and rushed, as if the writers were approaching some hard-and-fast 1h40 runtime target and needed to wrap things up quickly.

Review: I just love, love, love Matt Damon so much! I thought Stillwater was a really well-paced, emotional movie with an incredibly compelling story.

Name: Avatar: The Way of Water
Review: Spectacular in almost every way. I'm actually speechless at how good the visuals were. Like, first-in-class good. Every other blockbuster released this year should be ashamed of their CGI. It's complex enough to introduce new characters and world-building but that's about it. My biggest pain point, to be honest, was the dialogue; did they write it all in one afternoon? Again, not a massive problem because it's not the "point" of the movie, but it would've been nice for them to talk like actual people, especially in the action scenes. Oh, and you're seriously telling me they've had 13 years to work on this and nobody's found a better typeface to use for the exposition text than Papyrus!?

Name: Foxcatcher
Review: Foxcatcher definitely starts slow, but the initial commitment to a bit of character development and exposition is entirely worth it for the tense, eerie atmosphere that shrouds the rest of the movie, the growing tension hinting at inevitable tipping point, a culmination of all the events that came before it. There's lots to say about wealth and loneliness in this movie, as well as stark parallels that can be drawn between different characters and their desires for fame, stability, and recognition in the world. I'm glad I ended up enjoying this movie! Loved Steve Carell in this, too, even though I suppose he did technically very little acting. Less is more!

Name: Blade Runner 2049
Review: K had two girls in his apartment and he just stood there, terrified...he's just like me fr Jokes aside I'm so glad I decided to watch this for a third(!) time. I saw an Open Matte copy this time and had my eyes reopened at just how gorgeous every 👏 single 👏  frame of this movie is. The colours popped, the lighting slayed (slew?), and the cinematography and framing were just perfect. People often say that you can take almost any frame of this film and turn it into an A-Tier movie poster and they're goddamn right. And the sound design! Such a wonderful, enthralling, rich atmosphere is created by Zimmer & Wallfisch's incredible score, combined with this incredibly detailed, lived-in sound design that brings every single set piece to life. The fact that I can sit there at the end of the movie and feel like I've lived in 2049's world is awesome. I paid so much more attention to the story this time, too, where I'd previously just let the beautiful visuals wash over me. While it's definitely the weakest part of the movie for me, that doesn't mean it's weak. There's quite an expansive, thoughtful tale being told that starts simply and branches out into something more complex and rewarding by the end--and it gives the movie some great excuses to show off lots of different sets and sites in the process. It can be a bit slow at points but I almost wonder if the "aura" of the movie would be broken by trying to speed it up at all. Anyway, yeah, bumping this up half a star because I really had such a great time re-re-watching this!

Name: Oppenheimer
Review: Oppenheimer is a massive movie that demands a lot from its audience and I just kept thinking to myself in the cinema, while watching this beautiful movie, how lucky I was to be able to experience it in IMAX as God...I mean, Nolan, intended. Basically everything about the movie is perfect, I'd say. The 3 hour runtime is long, and I definitely felt it, but it's worth it for such an awesome crescendo of events, all branching off and building on each other, ultimately leading up to that moment with the final test. Speaking of, I don't think I've ever heard a cinema so quiet before; you could've heard a pin drop in the front row. Everyone was just completely transfixed on picture in front of them, waiting for the impending shockwave to blow us out of our seats. You know, I hate to say it, but I actually almost felt like I was there with the characters, witnessing the event firsthand. Everyone brought their A-game to this film, and I really, really hope Emily Blunt gets the recognition she deserves; maybe a Best Supporting Actress? Matt Damon is Matt Damon and I think he needs a mention for often bringing a bit of levity to such a heavy film; he's always good in his roles and I love the man. Ironically I don't have many strong feelings about Cillian Murphy's performance, one way or another! Good lord I want to fucking sob at how emphatic and powerful Göransson's soundtrack is, too. He already has such a stacked list of movies in his portfolio and this is just yet another, perfectly capturing the essence of the movie and translating it into a sound that fills every corner of the room and plays with emotions I didn't even know I had!

Name: 2001: A Space Odyssey
Review: OK I'll be really honest I don't see what's so special about the first half of this movie. I completely forgot how little dialogue there is and, at the risk of being ridiculed as someone who can't appreciate "real cinema", I'll admit I actually almost nodded off a few times...although that might've just been because the ambient space sounds were super relaxing and I haven't been sleeping enough lately. We had a brief intermission halfway through and then, all of a sudden, I felt so invested and interested in the story. There's no doubt that the HAL chapter and the psychedelic finale are the strongest sections of the film, both linked by their explorations of an intelligence which surpasses that of humankind, one seeking to destroy, and the other seeking to improve and evolve. And past that, I don't really know how much merit there is in trying to analyse this film. I don't think there's an adequate way to combine everything together in a way that doesn't leave something else out. You just have to sit there with everything and be content that it makes a really good movie.

Review: Still visually stunning and exactly what I want from a film adaptation of Dune. Casting is great and the sound design and soundtrack are so perfect too. The set design is so beautifully sci-fi yet still grounded in the medieval roots that run throughout the Dune franchise. However...I felt all that the first time and didn't have any new thoughts about it upon rewatching, so I struggled to enjoy it to the same degree. I think maybe it's the lack of relatability to the characters that's the rub for me here; I'll never be a Duke's son forced to wander a desert and ally with its native people to avenge my fallen house. I also got to see an early preview of a scene from Part 2, which was extremely exciting! My initial impression was that it had a very different tone to anything in the first movie, and I'm on the fence about whether that'll be a good or a bad thing. Guess I'll have to watch until March! TL;DR: Dune looks really nice on IMAX.

Name: Dune: Part Two
Review:
Everyone needs a hypeman like Stillgar.

It's very clear we're living through a special moment right now, where another great piece of literature has finally, properly been adapted for the screen, without compromising on runtime or sense of scale. The stars have aligned and Denis Villeneuve has been sent to guide us.

It's hard for me not to compare this movie to its older sibling, and I think this is where the rub lies with me at the moment. I really, really loved how precise and choreographed Part One was in its direction, and something about Part Two just felt rougher round the edges, and slightly more...detached? There are more character viewpoints to keep track of and it demands that the focus jumps around more to accommodate it.

I think I remember feeling similarly after reading the book, though, so maybe it's just a byproduct of having to adapt some much less straightforward material.

I still fully plan on seeing this a second time, which says a lot. I need another watch to fully appreciate the spectacle I just experienced.

The ending felt quite rushed and I would've liked for more of the questions to be developed and resolved. Instead the movie seems satisfied with taking a slightly easier route out, and I think it was a missed opportunity. I'll probably have the soundtrack on repeat all of tomorrow, though.

When you think that we're really just a bunch of animals blowing air through metal tubes and banging on wooden boxes...for something so beautiful to come from that is completely and utterly incredible.

I should go and practise my saxophone.

Name: Dune: Part Two
Review: I guess all it took was a second watch, and I'm happy to say I'm so back on the Dune 2 hype train, baby. I'm a wormpilled, sandmaxxing Fremcel to the core. Seriously though I think I was just stunned by my first watch because I enjoyed this one so much more and was able to devote so much more attention to the story and the acting, instead of just being bowled over by the incredible cinematography and set design. I saw Part 2 with Dolby Atmos audio this time, too, and what a difference to made. Night and day! It's so much easier to transport yourself to the surface of Arrakis when the wormsign actually, literally vibrates the room around you, and everything was just so much more immersive. My initial concerns over Stilgar's character having been used for comedic relief were also quashed this time, which I was extremely relieved about. Bardem's incredible performance felt so nuanced and definitely leant a lot further towards the "crazed fanatic" side than it did for me before. This is a man so desperately blinded by faith that he'd find the signs in just about anything if it meant there'd be a Messiah for him to follow. In a way I think he acted really well as a representation of the Fremen people as a whole, especially by the end of the movie. I'm really glad I went to see this a second time. I finally feel able to form an opinion on the movie because I could say after the first watch was, "I liked it," and any of my friends could tell you how unsure I came across when they asked me what I thought. This has definitely cemented Dune: Part 2 as one of my favourite movies. Also it's really embarrassing but there was a maybe 15-20 minute section in the middle of the film that I had absolutely no recollection of seeing before??? I'm not sure if I fell asleep or what but it was awesome to watch that for the first time!

Name: Longlegs
Review: Really loved what Perkins was going for in this movie but felt like it never escalated to the heights I was hoping for, and it ended more abruptly than I was expecting. The tiny cast and often empty, deserted sets created a really unsettling sense of isolation and helplessness that I loved. Take the opening scene, with the sea of identical, new-build houses on an estate stretching to infinity, or her log cabin home hidden deep in the woods. Awesome stuff. Nicholas Cage really pulled off something great with Longlegs the character, too. It's so close to silliness but ultimately a very creepy performance if you let yourself be scared by it. Maybe it could've been a little gorier or had more jumpscares to be the horror movie I was looking forward to. I think about 90% of it was pure setup for a "finale" which didn't really resolve anything 😬 Oh I thought the lightning was incredible though.

Name: Twisters
Review: Things I liked: - Glen Powell. This man is seriously charismatic and I totally agree that he's our best shot at a modern-day "movie star renaissance". - The tornados. Twisters positions itself as a natural disaster monster movie and I think it works really well. The mythos and reverence surrounding storm chasing is pretty infectious and I found myself thinking I'd probably watch that YouTube channel in real life. Things I didn't like: - The pair behind us who kept talking to each other for the duration of the film. - The three kids and dad to my left who held a running Q&A, at full volume, about who each character was and what their names were and why they were doing what they were doing. - The family to my right (after we moved seats) who all repeatedly took turns, individually, walking past the screen to leave the theatre from about the halfway mark until the credits rolled. - The mother who left her infant son alone in the cinema for the start of the movie and then returned, about 20 minutes in, with her phone flashlight on to search around for her seat and figure out where he was sitting. Like I feel super grumpy about it because I thought the movie was really fun but honestly people need to sit down and shut up if they're sharing a cinema with other people who've paid to be there.

Conversely, I actually found the jump to the reveal to be...too sudden? Like we're moseying along, piecing this puzzle together and than bam there it all is. And it's a depth of topic that I didn't really feel like the movie had earned. It's not a particularly serious movie and to—very quickly—try and wedge in something which is quite serious felt a bit wrong to me. Maybe it's the point that the (explained) motivations don't justify certain characters' actions, but I finding some way to add a few hints to that would've been cool. Aside from that, because there are positives to talk about, I thought it was still a pretty good movie. Naomi Ackie was very strong in her lead role, and Channing Tatum very convincingly plays an evil tech bro.

I really loved how self-referential and meta a lot of the scenes in this movie were and, combined with a staggering number of very cool stunts and practical gags, it really feels like the ode to stunt performers that I'm sure it wants to be—this is further reinforced with the behind the scenes shots during the credits, loved! A final spattering of random stuff: - Is this really Emily Blunt's normal accent?? - Aaron Taylor-Johnson doing a Matthew McConnaghey impression very well - You NEED....CARBS!!! - Alien robot voice changers are so funny - Waiting for a Director’s Cut with a full METALSTORM featurette Very good movie. Name: 28 Years Later
Review:
A fever dream of a movie in the best way. The choppy, frenetic editing and hyper-saturated look has only grown on me since I left the cinema.

Those same aspects definitely made it feel a bit rough around the edges at times, and I found myself wishing it could feel a bit more grounded in reality sometimes, only to promptly.change my mind and realise that, actually, this all makes it that much more interesting and fun to watch.

Very fleshed-out, lived in world. The set pieces and landscapes felt almost fantastical in a way, and I loved the occasional reminders that regular life was continuing on for everybody outside of the UK. They should probably quarantine us anyway, regardless of the zombies.

I didn't realise there was going to be a second (and even third!) part to this movie, so very excited to see that when it comes out!

Oh and it's hardly surprising but Ralph Fiennes stole the show for me. His stage presence is outstanding and he's a really great actor, is all I want to add.

Review:
Think the trailer was selling something very different to the movie. That's not to say I didn't enjoy the movie but it's always going to be a little disappointing when a set of expectations aren't met.

Anyway, sulk over. Lots to like here! The story is told in a particular way that really effectively builds the tension from multiple different angles at once. I actually cared about the characters and felt they were all given compelling motivations.

As with a lot of horror movies, it's at its best when we don't know what's going on and are only give the teeniest of peeks behind d the curtain. I don't think the ending fully landed for me but it was a very fun final few scenes! Are we allowed to laugh during horror movies? Genuinely funny in many places!
